headline: The AI trade cracked on financing costs rather than demand, sending the Nasdaq down 2.15 percent on Friday to its worst week since June, while the 10 year Treasury yield held near 5.10 percent and Brent crude stayed above 109 dollars.

summary.us: The S&P 500 fell 1.09 percent to 7,659.44, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.15 percent to 26,140.03 and the Dow slipped 0.34 percent to 52,002.41, leaving the S&P and Nasdaq with their worst week since June. The driver was the cost of funding AI infrastructure rather than demand for it, as CoreWeave five year credit default swaps hit a record intraday level near 1,194 basis points, Broadcom CEO Hock Tan warned that capital could become the industry's binding constraint, and the VIX climbed above 22 for the first time in four months.
summary.india: Indian benchmarks closed higher for a second straight session on Friday, with the Sensex up about 414 points and the Nifty near 23,146 as the IT index gained about 4 percent on Tech Mahindra's results, while mid and small caps finished roughly flat. The rupee ended at 94.89 per dollar for a sixth straight gain on RBI measures to curb spot dollar demand, recovering more than 2 percent from its 8 October record closing low of 96.88, though October FII outflows have reached about 49,935 crore rupees.
summary.global: Asia rebounded on Friday from Thursday's chip rout, with the Nikkei 225 up about 1.4 percent and the Hang Seng about 0.5 percent higher, after the KOSPI had fallen 7.57 percent on Thursday and triggered circuit breakers on both Korean boards. Brent crude held above 109 dollars on a US crude inventory draw of about 8.6 million barrels and Strait of Hormuz supply risk, gold sat near 4,187 dollars and the dollar index eased to about 101.8.

weekly.narrative: The week belonged to the cost of money rather than the promise of AI. Hot September CPI and PPI prints pushed fed funds futures toward pricing another quarter point increase by year end, and with the 10 year above 5 percent the market stopped asking whether AI compute is wanted and started asking who funds it: CoreWeave credit default swaps hit a record, the iShares Semiconductor ETF fell for eight straight sessions, and the Nasdaq shed 4.48 percent on the week while the Dow, carried by defensives, held a 0.67 percent gain. India went the other way, with the Nifty adding 3.44 percent as IT earnings landed well and the rupee rallied for six sessions on RBI intervention, even as October foreign outflows neared 50,000 crore rupees. Commodities split sharply, with WTI up 7.83 percent on a large US inventory draw and Strait of Hormuz risk while silver dropped 5.83 percent and gold was little changed, and crypto drifted lower on continued spot ETF outflows and close to a billion dollars of leveraged liquidations. Next week brings the 30,213 crore rupee Jio Platforms IPO, the largest in Indian history, alongside Tesla and Netflix earnings, Infosys on Friday and flash PMIs, all inside the Fed blackout that runs to the 28 October decision.
